## About

Kênia Barreiro de Souza is a professor at the Department of Economics at the Universidade Federal do Paraná (UFPR) where she has been a faculty member since 2016, and Vice-President of GeFam (Society of Family and Gender Economics) since 2025. She holds a PhD in Economics from the Universidade Federal de Minas Gerais (UFMG, 2015), with a sandwich period at the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign under the supervision of Professor Geoffrey Hewings (REAL/UIUC). She also holds a Master's degree in Applied Economics from the Universidade Federal de Juiz de Fora (UFJF, 2011).

Her research brings together computable general equilibrium modelling, input-output analysis, and labour economics to examine questions of gender inequality, regional disparities, and the macroeconomic effects of social policy. She is currently Vice-Coordinator of the PPGDE/UFPR Graduate Program and has served as a consultant for the International Labour Organization (ILO) in partnership with ECLAC and the Brazilian Secretariat for Care and Family.

## Research Interests

::: {.interests}

- Input-Output Analysis

- Environmental and Energy Economics
